subject: [PATCH v5 2/7] mm: allow shared folios to be promoted to a fast tier

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch allows shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios mapped by multiple processes to be promoted from slow memory to a faster tier, as long as the migration is from south to north. This change enables promotion for low-tier folios moving to top-tier, while maintaining existing restrictions for ordinary placement and non-promotion migrations. The patch also renames the `folio_use_access_time` function to `folio_numab_promotable` to better reflect its purpose.

reviews.author: Bharata Rao
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that this patch achieves the same effect as another patchset (pghot) in a more direct manner, and requested formal review with 'Reviewed-by' tag.
reviews.raw_body:
I am carrying a patch in pghot patchset to base this shared folio check
on @vma, in the async migration case where VMA won't be available to check the
exec permission. The effect of that is to allow promotion of shared exec folios.

This patch achieves the same in more direct manner.

Reviewed-by: Bharata B Rao <bharata@amd.com>

Regards,
Bharata.

2026-11-12.patch_summary: This patch allows shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios mapped by multiple processes to be promoted from slow memory to a faster tier, while maintaining existing restrictions for ordinary placement and non-promotion migrations. The patch renames the `folio_use_access_time` function to `folio_numab_promotable` to better reflect its purpose in handling memory-tiering and source-tier tests. This change enables promotion of low-tier folios to top-tier memory, but prevents east-west or north-to-south migrations. The patch addresses an issue with NUMA balancing that previously rejected shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios from being promoted.
